messages:
cheng: thinking out loud — i still worry about tenant interference with continuous batching. proposal: lane fencing + a small "escape hatch" queue for low-priority bursts so hot tenants can't starve background work

olivia: curious, what do you mean by 'fencing' here? per-tenant lanes with strict token caps?

cheng: yeah. basically allocate N lanes per device, each lane has a headroom token budget and an enqueue gating rule. if a tenant exceeds headroom we move new requests into the escape hatch (best-effort, slower path) or reject depending on policy

raj: are we talking hard limits or soft (credit decay) limits? hard limits are simpler but might cause p99 spikes if a tenant bursts within their burst window

maria: i like soft credits with decay + observable signals. we can expose metrics: lane_fill, escrow_tokens, escape_rate. then ops can tune policies per customer tier

sam: how does this interact with KV cache reuse and batching? if we fence lanes by tenant, we might lose coalescing benefits across tenants and hurt throughput

cheng: good point. idea is late-binding coalesce: we keep a small cross-lane coalescer for prefixes only — that preserves common prefix amortization without letting tail requests grab full batch slots. practical tradeoff: slightly more implementation complexity in runtime

olivia: can you sketch the config surface? e.g. what would an operator set per lane?

cheng: something like:
```
lane_config: [
  {name: "latency", capacity: 256, headroom_ms: 50, policy: "strict"},
  {name: "background", capacity: 128, headroom_ms: 200, policy: "best_effort"}
]
escape_hatch: {capacity: 64, routing: "deprioritize", preemption: "none"}
```

raj: we should define invariants: last_message_slo <= lane_headroom, and escape_hatch only used if lane_fill > capacity AND not violating p50 latency SLO

maria: what about preemption? do we evict in-flight batches or only prevent new enqueues? evicting in-flight is complex and may cause model state inconsistencies (kv cache)

cheng: prefer not to evict in-flight. instead: prevent new enqueues, accelerate draining with small priority bump to background lanes, and trigger autoscale if sustained

sam: autoscale tie-in is important. if escape_hatch usage > 10% for > 30s, trigger extra slots or route to cheaper model variant

olivia: who owns the policy decision: scheduler or control-plane? i want runtime to enforce fast decisions but control-plane to host the policy definitions and rollout targets

raj: agree. runtime should surface a compact policy contract: decisions are deterministic functions of (lane_config, current_fill, request_meta). control-plane pushes configs and records rollouts

maria: we'll need new metrics and dashboards. suggested: lane_fill{lane}, escape_rate{tenant}, blocked_enqueues{tenant}, coalesce_loss_ratio. also smoke tests to ensure we don't regress throughput

infra-bot: deploy-check: config-schema v1 passed local lint, integration tests pending

cheng: action items: (1) olivia to draft minimal policy schema (2) sam + raj to prototype escape_hatch path and autoscale signal (3) maria to add metrics + dashboard mocks. sync Wed 10am

olivia: ack, will have schema draft by EOD tomorrow :thumbsup:

raj: will start a small PoC branch for escape path — aim to demo next week

maria: i'll add metric stubs to the telemetry PR

cheng: thanks team. keeping this tight helps avoid complexity creep — prefer simpler soft-credit default, make strict fencing opt-in for enterprise tenants

sam: nit: add a short note about cost accounting when routing to cheaper variants (so billing isn't surprising)

cheng: good call. add to action items

olivia: thanks — closing thread, will follow with PR link soon
